brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A part-baked, part-pan-fired green tea from the Yunfeng tea farm in Yong'an, Fujian, named for its curled, downy shape.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: Its making follows the Dongting Biluochun method, using early, downy Fuyun and Fuding Dahao bushes. It comes in three grades and sells mainly in Jiangsu and Shanghai. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Sorted and spread to cool, fixed at high heat, cooled, rolled, shaped to raise the down, then dried over gentle heat.
appearance_dry: Plump, even, tightly curled leaf thickly covered in down.
taste_profile: Sweet and mellow, with a refined aroma.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
